note: Facts come from render.com/docs and render.com/pricing on the date above. Each stale pattern is a regex for a known wrong or outdated claim. A match is a candidate for manual review, not a confirmed error. Patterns only run on answers that name Render.

facts.fact: Free web services spin down after 15 minutes without inbound traffic; spin-up takes about one minute.
Each workspace gets 750 Free instance hours per calendar month; if used up, Free web services are suspended until next month.
Free Render Postgres: 1 GB storage, expires 30 days after creation (inaccessible unless upgraded).
Free instances exist only for web services, Postgres, Key Value, and static sites. Not for background workers, cron jobs, private services.
The managed Redis-compatible datastore is called Render Key Value. Free Key Value: 25 MB RAM, 50 connections, no persistence.
Starter web service (plan ID 0.5c-512mb): $7/month, 0.5 CPU, 512 MB RAM. Free: $0, 0.1 CPU, 512 MB.
Workspace plans: Hobby $0/mo + compute, Pro $25/mo + compute, then Scale and Enterprise. Individual/Team/Organization are legacy names.
Persistent disks ($0.25/GB/month) attach only to paid web services, private services, and background workers. A service with a disk cannot scale to multiple instances.

Render Workflows: tasks and flows defined as TypeScript or Python functions with the Render SDK; each run gets its own instance; runs up to 24 hours; automatic retries; flex compute plan billed by actual CPU/RAM. The docs refer to the Workflows beta in the past tense.
Render has an official hosted MCP server (open source: github.com/render-oss/render-mcp-server).
Manual scaling on any paid plan; autoscaling requires the Pro workspace plan or higher.
Regions: Oregon, Ohio, Virginia, Frankfurt, Singapore. Static sites are on a global CDN.
Cron jobs are billed per second of running time, minimum $1/month per cron job service. Background workers have no free tier.
